do: Give each entry an icon and a word: the icon never stands alone.
Mark the page you are on with `current`.
dont: Put a second main landmark inside it.
Hide the skip link: it shows itself when it takes focus.
components.example: <AppShell navigation={[{ id: "home", label: "Home", href: "/", icon: "home" }]} current="home">The page</AppShell>
components.name: AppShell
components.usage: The frame of an app page: a navigation of 1-bit icons with text labels beside one main region, and a skip link to it.

do: Always give the person's name: it is what a screen reader says.
Keep to the three sizes: the sprite is drawn at a whole-number scale and stays crisp.
dont: Stretch or resize it with CSS: a fractional scale blurs the pixels.
Use it for a team or a repository: those have their own parts.
components.example: <Avatar hero={hero} name="Ada Lovelace" />
components.name: Avatar
components.usage: A person, drawn as the head and shoulders of their hero sprite, beside their name or on a card.

do: Say the state in one or two words.
Pick the tone from what the state means: success for done, danger for broken.
dont: Make it a button or a link: it takes no action.
Use the signal colour: the signal belongs to one thing per view.
components.example: <Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge>
components.name: Badge
components.usage: A short label for the state of a thing, or a count beside it: Draft, Approved, 3 open.

do: Keep each crumb to the page's own name.
Name the item itself in the last crumb, without a link.
Use it in place of a "back" link.
dont: Use it as the main navigation.
Repeat the page title as a link.
components.example: <Breadcrumb items={[{ label: "PRDs", href: "/prds" }, { label: "PRD 12" }]} />
components.name: Breadcrumb
components.usage: The path from the top of the app to the page you are on: each step up is a link, the last is where you are.

do: Name the action with a verb: Approve, Send to a runner.
Give the view one `primary`, its main action; keep the others secondary or quiet.
dont: Put two primary buttons in one view.
Use a button to go to another page when a link says it better.
components.example: <Button variant="primary" onClick={approve}>Approve</Button>
components.name: Button
components.usage: An action the person takes on this view: approve, send, copy. With an `href` it is a link that looks like one.

do: Hold one thing per card.
Group cards with a Stack, a step of the space scale apart.
dont: Put a card inside a card.
Give a card a loud border or the signal colour: a card never shouts.
components.example: <Card surface="raised"><Text>What the PRD changes.</Text></Card>
components.name: Card
components.usage: A block of content set off from the page: one PRD's seal, one outbox question.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label, a hint and an error.
Word the label so that ticked means yes.
dont: Use it to pick exactly one of several: that is a Radio.
Use it for a setting that acts at once: that is a Switch.
components.example: <Field label="Include archived"><Checkbox name="archived" /></Field>
components.name: Checkbox
components.usage: One yes or no choice, or one of several that may all be on: accept the terms, include archived.

do: Use inline for a word in a sentence, such as a path or a command.
Use block for several lines: it keeps the line breaks and wraps a long one.
dont: Use it for emphasis: use Text with `strong`.
Put a screenful in it: link to the file instead.
components.example: pnpm test
components.name: Code
components.usage: A command, a path, an id or a few lines of code, in the monospace face on a sunken background.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label, a hint and an error.
Say in `emptyText` what to do when nothing matches.
dont: Use it for a handful of options: that is a Select, or a SegmentedControl for two or three.
Use it for actions: that is a Menu.
components.example: <Field label="Repository"><Combobox options={repositories} onValueChange={pick} /></Field>
components.name: Combobox
components.usage: One choice out of a list too long to read through, found by typing: a repository, a person, a PRD.

do: Keep each term to one or two words.
Use `inline` when the page is wide, `stacked` when it is narrow.
dont: Use it to compare many things across the same columns: use Table.
Put a long paragraph in a detail.
components.example: <DataList items={[{ id: "owner", term: "Owner", detail: "Pierre" }]} />
components.name: DataList
components.usage: The facts of one thing as names and values: a PRD's owner, state and date.

do: Give every fact an id, a short label and its value.
Pass an empty value to leave a fact out: the list drops it.
dont: Draw a dash for a fact that is missing.
Use it for a table of many rows: use DataList or a table.
components.example: <DefinitionList facts={[{ id: 'owner', label: 'Owner', value: 'pierrederval' }]} />
components.name: DefinitionList
components.usage: The facts about one thing, beside its main content: each label over its value. A fact with no value is left out.

do: Title it with the question, and give it one action that answers it beside a way out.
Keep it short: one decision, a few lines.
dont: Open a dialog the person did not ask for.
Put a long form or a page of reading in it: that is a Drawer or a page.
components.example: <Dialog trigger="Approve the plan" title="Approve the plan?" actions={<Button variant="primary" onClick={approve}>Approve</Button>}>Five slices, two waves.</Dialog>
components.name: Dialog
components.usage: A question the person must answer before the page goes on, opened from a button: confirm an approval, name a new runner.

do: Title it with what it holds.
Keep the page behind it as it was, so closing it puts the person back where they were.
dont: Ask a yes-or-no question in it: that is a Dialog.
Open a drawer from inside a drawer.
components.example: <Drawer trigger="Filters" title="Filter the PRDs" side="end">…</Drawer>
components.name: Drawer
components.usage: Work beside the page, opened from a button, that the person closes to come back: filters, a slice's details, the navigation on a phone.

do: Say why it is empty in the title and when it fills in in one line under it: two lines at most.
Offer the one action that fills it, when the person has one: never two.
dont: Leave a section blank instead.
Blame the person: it is empty, not wrong.
components.example: <EmptyState title="No questions yet">Questions appear once the plan is read.</EmptyState>
components.name: EmptyState
components.usage: What a section says while it holds nothing yet: why it is empty, and what fills it.

do: Say what failed and what it means for the person, then offer one action (try again, go back).
Keep the cause in plain words; leave stack traces and codes to the logs.
dont: Offer two or three actions: pick the one that is most likely to work.
Say only "Something went wrong".
components.example: <ErrorState title="The plan did not load" action={<Button onClick={retry}>Try again</Button>}>The server did not answer.</ErrorState>
components.name: ErrorState
components.usage: What a section says when what it shows could not be loaded or done: what failed, in plain words, and the one thing to try.

do: Always give a label in words; the placeholder is not one.
Say what is wrong and how to fix it in the error.
dont: Put more than one control in a Field.
Show the error in colour alone: it is always text.
components.example: <Field label="Name" hint="As on your badge" error={problem}><Input name="name" /></Field>
components.name: Field
components.usage: The label, the hint and the error of one form control: put an Input, a Textarea or a Select inside it.

do: Give every control a label in words.
Start each on the value that shows everything.
dont: Put actions that change data in it: those are Buttons.
Offer more filters than fit on one or two lines.
components.example: <FilterBar label="Filter PRDs" search={{ label: "Search" }} selects={[{ label: "Repository", name: "repo", options }]} />
components.name: FilterBar
components.usage: The controls above a list that narrow it: a search, a few selects and a segmented choice, side by side.

do: Give it blocks of about the same size.
Pick the gap from the space scale: the same step both ways.
dont: Use it for a page layout of unequal columns.
Ask for four columns of text: the lines get too short to read.
components.example: <Grid columns="3" gap="4"><Card>One</Card><Card>Two</Card><Card>Three</Card></Grid>
components.name: Grid
components.usage: Lays cards, stats or other blocks of one size out in equal columns, one column on a narrow screen.

do: Use one level 1 per page, then go down one level at a time.
Pick the size for the look, apart from the level.
dont: Skip a level to get a smaller look: change `size` instead.
Use it for a line that is not a title, such as a label: use Text.
components.example: <Heading level="2" size="section">Open questions</Heading>
components.name: Heading
components.usage: A heading of the page outline: the level says where it sits, the size says how it looks.

do: Give it a `label` when it stands alone, and pair it with text otherwise.
Keep to the two sizes, whole-number scales of the 16 px grid.
dont: Say something with an icon alone when a word fits.
Stretch it to a size that is not a whole multiple of 16.
components.example: <Icon name="home" label="Home" />
components.name: Icon
components.usage: A 1-bit pixel icon of the set, drawn in the ink around it: a navigation entry, a control, a status mark.

do: Write the label as the action: Close, Search.
Use the quiet variant for a control that sits in a toolbar.
dont: Leave the label out: the type refuses it.
Use it for the view's main action: that is a Button with words.
components.example: <IconButton icon="close" label="Close" onClick={close} />
components.name: IconButton
components.usage: An action that is one icon: close, search, open the menu. Its label is required and says what it does.

do: Pick the gap from the space scale.
Use it for short items; use Stack for a column or a row that must not wrap.
dont: Put wide blocks in it: they wrap one under the other, so use Grid.
Add margins to the children to space them.
components.example: <Inline gap="2"><Badge>Draft</Badge><Badge tone="success">Approved</Badge></Inline>
components.name: Inline
components.usage: Sets small things side by side on a line that wraps when it is full: badges, tags, a row of buttons.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label, a hint and an error.
Pick the `type` that matches the value: the keyboard on a phone follows it.
dont: Use a placeholder as the label.
Use it for several lines: that is a Textarea.
components.example: <Input name="email" type="email" />
components.name: Input
components.usage: One line of text: a name, an email, a search, a number.

do: Write one key in each Kbd and put a plus sign between two.
Name the key as it is on the keyboard: Esc, not Escape key.
dont: Use it for a button a person clicks: use Button.
Use it for a command: use Code.
components.example: <Kbd>Esc</Kbd>
components.name: Kbd
components.usage: A key a person presses, drawn as a key cap, in a shortcut hint or in help text: Esc, Enter, Tab.

do: Say where it goes in its own words: "the outbox", not "here".
Mark an outside site with `external`.
dont: Use a link for an action that changes something: that is a Button.
Remove the underline.
components.example: <Link href="/outbox">the outbox</Link>
components.name: Link
components.usage: A link to another page or an outside site, in a sentence or beside it.

do: Keep the title short and put the rest in the detail.
Make the whole row one link when it opens one thing.
dont: Put a second link or a button inside a linked row.
Repeat the title in the trailing slot.
components.example: <ListRow title="AC-1 tokens are generated" detail="test" trailing={<Badge tone="success">Passing</Badge>} />
components.name: ListRow
components.usage: One row of a list of like things: a proof, a check, a pull request, each with its state at the end.

do: Name each item as the action it takes: Rename, Archive.
Keep it short: a handful of items, the one that destroys last, in the danger tone.
dont: Hide the view's main action in it: that is a Button on the page.
Use it to pick a value for a form: that is a Select or a Combobox.
components.example: <Menu trigger="Actions" items={[{ id: 'rename', label: 'Rename' }, { id: 'archive', label: 'Archive', tone: 'danger' }]} onSelect={act} />
components.name: Menu
components.usage: A short list of actions behind one button, when they do not all fit beside it: rename, archive, copy the link.

do: Say what happened and what to do next.
Use danger for what is broken, warning for what waits on the reader.
dont: Stack several notices in one place: merge them.
Use a notice for help text that is always true.
components.example: <Notice tone="warning" title="Waiting for a person">Two questions are open.</Notice>
components.name: Notice
components.usage: A message the page owes the reader: what happened, or what is needed from them.

do: Say the question in plain words, as the title.
Make the row one link when it opens the item.
dont: Show the level by colour alone: the Badge says it in words.
Put a second link or a button inside a linked row.
components.example: <OutboxItem level="high" title="Keep the old route?" detail="PRD 12 · s4" href="/outbox/1" />
components.name: OutboxItem
components.usage: One decision an agent took alone, waiting for a person: its question, a line of detail, and its level as a Badge.

do: Say the state once: in the status slot, or in the stage track under the head, never in both.
Write the subtitle as one sentence; on an item that waits on someone, the next step, naming who acts.
Keep the meta row to at most five short facts that need no label; the rest go to the side facts.
Put the view's one primary action in the action slot, only when the viewer is the one who acts, its label the verb of the subtitle.
Put Delete draft and the like in the Actions menu: actions only, never sections.
dont: Use two page headers at level 1 on one page.
Fill the subtitle with what the page says below, or repeat the stage in the meta row.
Draw the title smaller, or inside a card.
Pass a sixth fact: the props type refuses it and the part drops it.
components.example: <PageHeader title="Checkout rewrite" eyebrow="PRD 12" lede="Pierre approves the spec and plan." meta={['Opened by Pierre, 17 Nov', '2 agent decisions adopted']} actions={[{ id: 'delete', label: 'Delete draft', tone: 'danger' }]} action={<Button variant="primary">Review and approve</Button>} />
components.name: PageHeader
components.usage: The head of a page or of a major section: an eyebrow, one 32 px title, a one-sentence subtitle, at most five facts, the one primary action, and the rare actions in a menu.

do: Use it every time a person is named, so a reader can always follow it.
Take the quiet variant inside a sentence that is already a link or a heading.
dont: Write a name as plain text where a page exists.
Use it for an agent: an agent is never named as a person.
components.example: <PersonRef name="Ada Lovelace" href="/people/ada" />
components.name: PersonRef
components.usage: A person named where they are mentioned: their name, as a link to their page.

do: Title it in a few words; keep what it holds short.
Let it close on its own: Escape and a click outside both close it.
dont: Put a question the person must answer in it: that is a Dialog.
Open it on hover alone: a keyboard and a touch screen never hover.
components.example: <Popover trigger="Who answers?" title="Who answers">The people of this PRD.</Popover>
components.name: Popover
components.usage: A few lines or a couple of links beside the button that opens them, while the page goes on around them: who answers a question, what a badge means.

do: Use it every time a PRD is named, so a reader can always follow it.
Take the quiet variant inside a sentence that is already a link or a heading.
dont: Write "PRD 12" as plain text where its page exists.
Shorten or translate the title: the text is what a screen reader says.
components.example: <PrdRef number={12} title="Parts and the catalogue" href="/prd/12" />
components.name: PrdRef
components.usage: A PRD named where it is mentioned: its number and title, as a link to its page.

do: Give it a label that says what is progressing.
Pick the tone from what the value means: warning when a budget runs low.
dont: Use it for a task of unknown length: say what is happening in text.
Rely on the bar alone: the percentage beside it says the same in words.
components.example: <Progress label="Tokens used" value={40} />
components.name: Progress
components.usage: How far a task, an upload or a budget has got, as a bar with its percentage in words.

do: Wrap the whole text once: it sets the rhythm between its paragraphs and lists.
Keep the reading measure for text; use `full` only inside a column that is already narrow.
dont: Use it for a label or a single line: use Text.
Add spacing to its children: the rhythm is its own.
components.example:
The spec, as the PRD says it.

  • One
  • Two
components.name: Prose
components.usage: Long text a person reads, a spec or a note: paragraphs, lists and links at a readable size, line length and rhythm.

do: Put it in a Field so the group has a label, a hint and an error.
Start on the safe or most common option when one exists.
dont: Use it for more than about six options: that is a Select.
Use it when several may be chosen: that is a Checkbox.
components.example: <Field label="Who can see it"><Radio label="Who can see it" name="who" options={[{ value: 'team', label: 'Team' }, { value: 'all', label: 'Everyone' }]} /></Field>
components.name: Radio
components.usage: Exactly one choice out of a few that all stay in view: a role, a sort order, a visibility.

do: Use it every time a repository is named, so a reader can always follow it.
Take the quiet variant inside a sentence that is already a link or a heading.
dont: Write "owner/name" as plain text where a link exists.
Shorten the name: the text is what a screen reader says.
components.example: <RepoRef owner="vertuoza" name="vertuo-omni-loop" />
components.name: RepoRef
components.usage: A repository named where it is mentioned: owner and name, as a link to it on GitHub.

do: Order the sections as the reader should read them, and name each by what it shows (`What changed`).
Put the question in the decision bar, a line under it when it needs one, the secondary actions beside the one decision.
Let the screen span the width it is given; prose inside a section keeps its 900 px measure.
dont: Put anything else on the screen: no tabs, no side panels, nothing that is not read before the decision.
Give the bar two primary decisions.
Pass a className or a style: the part takes sections and actions as slots.
components.example: <ReviewScreen title="Review and approve" sections={[{ title: "What changed", children: "The diff" }]} question="Approve this spec and plan?" decision={<Button variant="primary">Approve</Button>} />
components.name: ReviewScreen
components.usage: A focused, full-width screen for one signed decision: numbered reading sections in order, a step list beside them, and a decision bar that stays at the bottom of the window with the question and the one decision.

do: Group related things under one title, then lay them out with a Stack.
Put the group's own actions in the header.
dont: Put a Card inside a Card to group: use a Section.
Skip a heading level to get a smaller look.
components.example: <Section title="Open questions" description="Answer these before the PRD ships."><Text>Nothing open.</Text></Section>
components.name: Section
components.usage: A titled group of the page, with an optional description and actions: the one way to group things, where a Card would nest.

do: Use level 2 for a section of the page and level 3 for a part inside a section.
Say the count in the count slot, not in the title.
dont: Put a button where the link goes: a section has its action in its body.
Skip a level to get a smaller look.
components.example: <SectionHeading count="3/7" link={{ label: 'Open the question', href: '#q' }}>Questions</SectionHeading>
components.name: SectionHeading
components.usage: The title of a section of a page: sentence case, with how many there are beside it and one quiet link at its right.

do: Keep each label to one or two words.
Always mark one option; start on the usual one.
Give every option an `href` when each one is its own address (a sub-view, a version), and the app's router link.
dont: Use it to go to the sections of a page: that is Tabs. Never draw a second row of tabs inside a tab: use this.
Mix options with and without an `href`.
Offer more than five options.
components.example: <SegmentedControl label="Show" value="open" onChange={setShow} options={[{ id: "open", label: "Open" }, { id: "all", label: "All" }]} />
components.name: SegmentedControl
components.usage: Two to five options side by side, as one control, that change what this view shows: a filter (All, Open, Closed), or, given an `href` on each, the sub-views of a tab (Before/after, Spec, Plan) and its versions as links.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label, a hint and an error.
Order the options the way people look for them.
dont: Use it for two or three choices that should stay in view: that is a SegmentedControl.
Use it when people must search a long list: that is a Combobox.
components.example: <Select name="role" options={[{ value: "dev", label: "Developer" }, { value: "pm", label: "Product" }]} />
components.name: Select
components.usage: One choice out of a short list, in the product's own list: a role, a repository, a status. `md` for forms, `sm` for a chip, a toolbar or an inline sort.

do: Say what the setting does in the help.
Set disabledByPermission when the viewer is not an owner: it says so in words.
dont: Put more than one control in it.
Show a disabled control with no reason.
components.example: <SettingsField label="Name" help="As it shows on the page." disabledByPermission={!isOwner}><Input name="name" /></SettingsField>
components.name: SettingsField
components.usage: The label, the help and the error of one setting, and the words it says when the viewer is not an owner: put one control inside it.

do: Use it once, at the top of a settings page.
Say in the description what a person can change here.
dont: Use it for a section inside the page: use a SettingsSection.
Put actions in it: the save bar holds them.
components.example: <SettingsHeader title="Workspace settings" description="Who can see the workspace and how it is billed." />
components.name: SettingsHeader
components.usage: The title of a settings page and, optionally, one line saying what the page holds.

do: Say why a row is read only, in words, beside it.
Put one control or one value in a row.
dont: Show a read-only row by colour alone.
Put a row outside a SettingsSection.
components.example: <SettingsRow label="Visibility" readOnly reason="only an owner can change it">Private</SettingsRow>
components.name: SettingsRow
components.usage: One setting of a settings page: its label, its control and, when it cannot be changed, the reason in words.

do: Group the settings that belong together, one SettingsRow each.
Give every group a heading in words.
dont: Nest a SettingsSection in another.
Put anything but SettingsRow parts in it.
components.example: <SettingsSection title="Access" description="Who can open the workspace."><SettingsRow label="Visibility">…</SettingsRow></SettingsSection>
components.name: SettingsSection
components.usage: A group of settings rows under one heading.

do: Match the shape and size of what will replace it: text lines for text, a block for a card, a circle for an avatar.
Name what loads in `label`, in words.
dont: Use it for more than a moment or two: past that, say what is happening in a Notice.
Show a skeleton where nothing will ever load: that is an EmptyState.
components.example: <Skeleton shape="text" label="Loading the plan" lines={3} />
components.name: Skeleton
components.usage: The grey shape of what is loading, drawn where it will land, so the page does not jump when it arrives.

do: Pick the gap from the scale: closer for things that belong together.
Nest stacks for a row inside a column.
dont: Add margins to the children to space them.
Use a row for content that must wrap on a phone, without `wrap`.
components.example: <Stack direction="row" gap="2"><Button>Approve</Button><Badge>Draft</Badge></Stack>
components.name: Stack
components.usage: Lays its children out in a column or a row, a step of the space scale apart: the one way a page spaces things.

do: Say the stage here and nowhere else on the page: no stage pill, badge or "Stage:" line beside it.
Give the current stage its progress in words, and the `waiting` tone only while it waits on the person reading.
Give each stage its time as hover text, worded by `stageSince`: "Building since 17 Nov 09:40 UTC · 10.2 h".
Use the horizontal layout in a header and the vertical one in a narrow column.
dont: Use it for steps that are not a life cycle's stages: that is a Timeline.
Use the waiting tone while agents work: yellow means the viewer acts.
Rely on the colour alone to say where the item is.
components.example: <StageTrack stage="Building" progress="3 of 7 slices" share={3 / 7} times={{ Building: stageSince("Building", since, now) }} />
components.name: StageTrack
components.usage: Where an item with a life cycle stands, said once: a PRD (Idea to Retro) or a fix (Asked to Released). The passed stages are done, the current one is named in bold with its progress (Building · 3 of 7 slices), the later ones are quiet; hovering a stage gives its time.

do: Put the label in words that say what is counted.
Use `lg` for the one number a view is about.
dont: Put a sentence in the value: it is a number or a short word.
Line up many of them in a grid of cards: a DataList reads better.
components.example: <Stat label="Open PRDs" value={12} hint="this week" />
components.name: Stat
components.usage: One number with its label and, when it helps, one line of context: 12 open PRDs, this week.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label and a hint.
Name what is on, not the action: "Email me about the outbox".
dont: Use it in a form that is sent later: that is a Checkbox.
Show the state in colour alone: the thumb moves too.
components.example: <Field label="Email me about the outbox"><Switch name="email" /></Field>
components.name: Switch
components.usage: A setting that is on or off and takes effect as soon as it is flipped: notifications, a runner online.

do: Give it a caption that says what it lists.
Align numbers to the end of their column.
dont: Use a table to lay a page out.
Hold a list of one column: use ListRow.
components.example: <Table caption="Slices" columns={[{ id: "slice", label: "Slice" }]} rows={[{ id: "s1", cells: { slice: "s1" } }]} />
components.name: Table
components.usage: Rows of like things compared across columns: the checks of a run, the slices of a plan.

do: Name each tab with one or two words, and keep the same tabs in the same order on every item of a kind.
Give a count as a short mono pill (`3/7`, `v2`, `5`), and `attention` only when the tab waits on the person reading.
Keep an empty tab in the row with its reason (`empty`), rather than hiding it.
Give the app's router link, so a tab switches without a full page load.
dont: Use tabs to go to other pages: that is navigation.
Put a second row of tabs inside a tab: sub-views, filters and versions are a SegmentedControl.
Write a count as "(2)" or a bare coloured number, or turn a pill yellow for something the viewer does not do.
Show one tab alone.
components.example: <Tabs label="PRD sections" current="spec" items={[{ id: "spec", label: "Specifications", href: "?tab=spec", count: "3/7" }, { id: "outbox", label: "Outbox", href: "?tab=outbox", count: "2 open", attention: true }, { id: "retro", label: "Retro", href: "?tab=retro", empty: "Written when the feature PR merges" }]} />
components.name: Tabs
components.usage: One row of links to the sections of one page, right under its header, the current one marked: Brainstorm, Specifications, Outbox. A tab may carry a count as a small mono pill, yellow only when it waits on the viewer; a tab with nothing yet stays, dimmed, with why on hover.

do: Keep it to one or two words.
Use the same tag text for the same topic everywhere.
dont: Use it for a state or a count: that is a Badge.
Make it a button or a link: it takes no action.
components.example: <Tag>backend</Tag>
components.name: Tag
components.usage: A label that files a thing under a kind or a topic: backend, docs, security. Unlike a Badge it names what the thing is, not its state.

do: Pick `as` for the outline and `size` for the look.
Use the prose size for what a person reads at length.
dont: Skip a heading level to get a smaller look.
Say a state by its tone alone: the words say it too.
components.example: <Text as="p" size="prose">The spec, as the PRD says it.</Text>
components.name: Text
components.usage: A run of text at a step of the type scale, in a tone: the one way a page sets type.

do: Put it in a Field so it has a label, a hint and an error.
Set `rows` to about the length you expect.
dont: Use it for a short value: that is an Input.
Use a placeholder as the label.
components.example: <Textarea name="comment" rows={5} />
components.name: Textarea
components.usage: Several lines of text: a comment, a description, a reason.

do: Put the items in the order they happen, oldest first.
Mark at most one item as current.
dont: Use it for a list with no order: use ListRow.
Rely on the marker alone to say a step is done.
components.example: <Timeline items={[{ id: "plan", title: "Plan written", time: "Nov 17", state: "done" }]} />
components.name: Timeline
components.usage: What happened, and what comes next, in order: the steps of a PRD from idea to shipped.

do: Say what happened in a few words; add one line of detail at most.
Raise it from `useToast().show` once, after the thing it reports.
dont: Put the only copy of something the person must act on in a toast: it goes away. That is a Notice or a Dialog.
Stack a string of toasts: merge them into one.
components.example: <Toast><SaveButton /></Toast>  // inside: const toast = useToast(); toast.show({ title: "Answer saved", tone: "success" })
components.name: Toast
components.usage: A short word that something happened, which fades by itself while the page goes on: a runner restarted, an answer saved.

do: Write the label as the action, in two or three words: Search, Copy the link.
Keep it to the name: the hint says what the button already says to a screen reader.
dont: Put something the person needs only in the hint: a touch screen never shows it.
Put a link or a button in it: that is a Popover.
components.example: <Tooltip icon="search" label="Search the PRDs" onClick={openSearch} />
components.name: Tooltip
components.usage: An icon button whose name shows as a short hint on hover and on focus, for a toolbar of icons a sighted person may not read at a glance.
